LTF0726(1) Item 18 Morris Street, Summer Hill - Request for resident parking to both sides of the street. (Djarrawunang-Ashfield Ward/Summer Hill Electorate/Burwood PAC). SUMMARY A Notice of Motion was raised in the Council meeting on the 28 October 2025 to investigate resident requests (via petition) to have restricted (resident) parking placed to both sides of Morris Street, Summer Hill. This in turn-initiated parking occupancy surveys to be carried out in Morris Street between Smith Street and Junction Road and the adjoining streets of Moonbie Street and Nowranie Street to determine parking space availability at particular days and periods of the year and assess whether added resident parking be introduced based on the Council’s ‘Public Domain Parking Policy’. OFFICERS RECOMMENDATION That: 1. The current Resident Parking Scheme arrangement for Morris Street not be extended to both sides of the street, and 2. A review of Morris Street parking usage and any possible extension to the current scheme be undertaken when parking for the Summer Hill precinct area is reviewed. LTF ADVICE Public speakers Dominic Ogburn and Jules Francois entered the room at 11:21am Ms Francois and Mr Ogburn raised concerns about long-term parking on Morris Street, particularly near Smith Street and Lackey Street where parking demand is high. They advised that several vehicles, including large vehicles, trailers and a campervan, had been parked for extended periods and that some nearby residents or businesses appeared to be using unrestricted parking to store multiple vehicles. The speakers stated that these parking practices have reduced parking availability for residents and visitors. Ms Francois advised that she had difficulty parking near her home and, due to mobility issues, sometimes needed to make several trips from nearby streets when unloading items. Mr Ogburn advised that he had helped initiate a petition seeking resident parking restrictions and stated that, in his view, there was strong local support for changes. He requested that the unrestricted side of Morris street be converted to a two-hour resident parking restriction on weekdays to improve turnover and reduce long-stay parking by non-residents, commuters and nearby businesses. Public Speakers Dominic Ogburn and Jules Francois left the meeting at 11:26am Forum members and Council officers discussed the existing scheme, including the operation of the weekday two-hour restriction and reported difficulty parking on the unrestricted side of the street. Council officers advised that parking demand in Morris Street is highest closer to the Summer Hill shops, while sections further from the shops have lower utilisation. Officers noted that the existing restricted side of Morris Street continues to provide turnover, but more permits have been issued for the street than there are available parking spaces. Council officers suggested that parking pressure are partly generated by residents’ own vehicles, rather than only by external demand. The Chairperson raised concerns about the issuing of a parking permit for a campervan that is parked often in Morris Street. Council officers noted that the subject campervan would be a registered vehicle and that permits should not be issued to trucks, caravans and trailers. Officers also noted that extending the Resident Parking Scheme to both sides of Morris Street may not resolve the issue and could shift parking demand into nearby streets, which also experience high occupancy in locations closer to the shopping strip. Any further changes should therefore be considered as part of a broader precinct review rather than in isolation. The Chairperson advised that Point 2 of the recommendation be amended advising that Council will consider a review of Morris Street parking usage and any possible extension to the current scheme including a parking plan for the surrounding streets be undertaken when parking for the Summer Hill precinct area is reviewed. RECOMMENDATION That: 1. The current Resident Parking Scheme arrangement for Morris Street not be extended to both sides of the street, and 2. That Council consider a review of Morris Street parking usage and any possible extension to the current Resident Parking Scheme as part of a broader study of parking in the Summer Hill Precinct including a parking plan for the surrounding streets. General Business: Item 19 - Webbs Avenue Ashfield – Request for line marked parking bays The Chairperson tabled correspondence from a resident regarding parking behaviour in Webbs Avenue, Ashfield. The correspondence raised concerns that, between two street trees where two vehicles can ordinarily park, a resident has been moving one vehicle into the centre of the available space to reserve the second parking space. The request sought line marking of the two parking bays, with appropriate signage indicating that vehicles must park within the marked bays. Council Officers advised that the request would be investigated. Item 20 – Illawarra Road, Marrickville The Representative for the Member of Summer Hill requested that Council consider an education campaign to explain the purpose of honeycomb road markings, which are used to alert drivers to a change in the road environment, including potential speed environment changes. It was noted that honeycomb markings had recently been installed on some streets as part of high pedestrian activity area treatments, and that some community members may not understand their meaning. Council officers advised that the markings are intended as a threshold treatment to alert road users that they are entering a changed road environment. Officers noted that the markings themselves do not create a legal speed requirement; the posted speed signs remain the legal control. Council officers also advised that the request would be reviewed and that options for community education, including social media messaging, would be considered. Item 21 – Marlborough Street, Leichhardt The Representative for the Member of Balmain raised concerns about inconsistent speed signage on Marlborough Street, Leichhardt, near Norton Street. It was noted that a variable message sign currently displays a 40km/h speed limit; however, the existing fixed street signs still display a 50km/h speed limit. C ouncil officers advised that the matter would be investigated. Item 22 – Grosvenor Crescent / Elizabeth Street, Summer Hill – Cycleway Investigation The Inner West Bicycle Coalition representative queried the status of a previous Council resolution to investigate a cycleway along Grosvenor Crescent and Elizabeth Street, between the Smith Street roundabout and the Ashfield Aquatic Centre. It was noted that the key area of concern is the uphill section of Grosvenor Crescent from Smith Street to Dover Street, where it is considered that a cycleway could improve safety and connectivity for people cycling through the corridor and deter parking of caravans on this section of road. Members discussed whether the route is included in Council’s cycling planning documents or action plan, including any high-priority routes. It was suggested that, if the route is not currently identified, it should be reviewed for possible inclusion. Council officers also advised that the matter would be checked with the relevant strategic cycling planning team to confirm whether the route is already included in Council’s cycle planning documents and, if not, whether it should be considered for future investigation. Meeting closed at 12:25pm. CHAIRPERSON Clr Victor Macri

LTF0826(1) Item 1 Proposed EV kerbside charging locations (ALL WARDS / ALL ELECTORATES / ALL PACS) SUMMARY Council is committed to supporting and encouraging the use of electric vehicles (EVs) in the Inner West. Following the adoption of “Powering Ahead”, Council’s Electric Vehicle Encouragement Strategy in 2023, Council has partnered with several Kerbside charging providers and has been successful in gaining State Government Funding for the provision of Kerbside EV charging. The current rollout of chargers will be installed by EVX. This work is being delivered under the Transport and Infrastructure State Environmental Planning Policy, which allows them to install chargers without a development application. To ensure EV owners can easily use the chargers, Council is proposing to establish ‘No Parking 8am–10pm EV excepted while charging’ zones at a number of charging sites. Targeted engagement has been undertaken, and a summary of the engagement outcomes has been provided with associated recommendations and signage and line marking plans. OFFICERS RECOMMENDATION That the proposed EV charging sites at the following locations (and as shown in the signage and line marking plans (provided in Attachment 1) be approved as ‘No Parking 8am-10pm EV excepted while charging’ spaces ; 1. War Memorial Park - 39 Moore Street Leichhardt (ELP Pole in Catherine Street) 2. Hinsby Park Playground (ELP Pole in Piper Street South) 3. 56 Robert Street Balmain (Between Mullens St and Buchanan St) 4. 1 Goodsell St, St Peters 5. Camdenville Park – ELP Pole at Opposite 74 May Street St Peters LTF ADVICE The Representative for the Member of Balmain confirmed the minutes from the previous meeting and noted that the current item was consistent with the previous discussion. The representative for the member in Balmain asked whether the proposed charging location at 39 Moore Street is the only location being considered in and around this area. Council Officer advised that they would confirm. The representative for the member in Summer Hill asked whether there was a charging spaces would be available for general parking when not being used for charging and whether there was a specific commercial/revenue arrangement. The Forum members agreed with the recommendation. Camdenville Park – ELP Pole at Opposite 74 May Street St Peters LTF0826(1) Item 2 Trafalgar Lane, Annandale - Proposed 'No Parking Zone' adjacent to No. 219 and No. 217 Trafalgar Street ( BALUDARRI- BALMAIN WARD/BALMAIN ELECTORATE/LEICHHARDT PAC) SUMMARY Council has received concerns regarding vehicle access to the rear of properties in Trafalgar Lane, Annandale. An assessment was undertaken to several locations within the lane, and while some locations may benefit from a ‘No Parking’ zone, it is recommended that these locations be reviewed if more submissions are received from impacted residents. As on-street parking supply is deemed important for residents and considering that there has not been significant concerns received from other sections of Trafalgar Lane, it is recommended that at this time a ‘No Parking’ zone in Trafalgar Lane be introduced opposite Nos. 217 and 219 Trafalgar Street, Annandale. While residents value the importance of on-street parking supply, ‘No Parking’ zones opposite properties Nos. 254, 221, and 149 Trafalgar Street at this time is recommended to be supported in-principle and implemented only if additional requests are received, and supported from a separate community consultation. OFFICERS RECOMMENDATION That: 1. A 9.6m ‘No Parking’ zone on the eastern side of Trafalgar Lane, Annandale, opposite Nos. 217 and 219 Trafalgar Street be approved. 2. Considering the importance of on-street parking supply, ‘No Parking’ zones opposite properties Nos. 254, 221, and 149 Trafalgar Street be supported in-principle and implemented if additional requests are received, and supported from a separate community consultation. LTF ADVICE Public speakers Lola Davidson, Damien Prentice, Ludvik entered the meeting at 11:03am Mr Prentice outlined concerns regarding vehicle access to garages in Trafalgar Lane and advised that manoeuvring vehicles can be difficult when cars are parked opposite driveway access points. He noted that on-street parking demand in the area is high and expressed concern regarding the extent of the proposed ‘No Parking’ restrictions and the potential loss of parking opportunities for residents. Mr Ludvik raised concerns regarding the loss of convenient parking for residents, visitors and tradespeople. He advised that parking demand in the surrounding area is already significant and suggested that the proposal may reduce available parking supply without addressing broader parking pressures within the locality. Public speakers Lola Davidson, Damien Prentice and Ludvik left the meeting at 11:18am Public speakers Bharat Pandya (on behalf of Vivek) and Craig entered the meeting at 11:19am Mr Craig supported the proposal and commented on the challenges associated with vehicle access and manoeuvring within the lane when vehicles are parked opposite garage driveways. He considered the proposed restrictions to be a reasonable measure to improve access while maintaining the overall function of the lane. Mr Pandya supported the proposal and advised that difficulties accessing garages had existed for a number of years. He noted that attempts to resolve the issue between affected residents had not resulted in a satisfactory outcome and considered the proposed restrictions necessary to maintain access. Public speakers Bharat Pandya (on behalf of Vivek) and Craig left the meeting at approximately 11:25am. Council officers explained that the general traffic assessment considers parking restrictions where laneways are narrow, while individual site conditions are assessed separately. Forum members raised concerns regarding the proposed history of the garage access issues, the width of the lane, vehicle maneuvering requirements, and the potential impact on parking supply. Questions were raised regarding the timing of the double-garage development, and it was confirmed that the development had been constructed in 2022. Members also discussed whether an alternative or reduced restriction could provide an appropriate compromise while maintaining access to affected properties. Council Officer provided further information regarding the assessment undertaken, including the width of Trafalgar Lane, vehicle maneuvering requirements, parking demand and relevant traffic engineering considerations. LTF0926(1) Item 1 Final Draft Birchgrove-Balmain East LATM Study (Baludarri-Balmain Ward/Balmain Electorate/Leichhardt PAC) SUMMARY Council has prepared the final draft Local Area Traffic Management (LATM) study to address key community concerns about traffic, pedestrian and cycling facilities in the Birchgrove-Balmain East LATM precinct area. The recommendations aim to align with Council policies and strategies, with an emphasis on improving pedestrian and cyclist movements, whilst retaining safe and acceptable traffic volume and speeds in local streets. OFFICERS RECOMMENDATION 1. 1. That the Final Draft Birchgrove-Balmain East Local Area Traffic Management (LATM) Study be endorsed for community consultation. 2. 2. That the report be placed on Public Exhibition, providing a minimum 28 days for community feedback and the results be reported back to the Local Transport Forum. LTF ADVICE Public Speaker Tim Hand entered the meeting at 11:11am Tim Hand welcomed the overall direction of the study, particularly its focus on road safety, speed reduction and traffic calming measures. He considered the consultation process thorough and supportive of safer transport outcomes for the precinct. Tim Hand sought clarification regarding the timing of the public exhibition process and the anticipated implementation of high-priority projects. Council officers advised that public exhibition was expected to occur between late November and late December 2026, with the intention of concluding prior to the Christmas period. Officers further explained that, if endorsed by Council in 2027, priority projects would proceed through the capital works process, including detailed design, funding allocation and construction programming. It was noted that the projects are not currently funded and that Council will continue pursuing State and Commonwealth funding opportunities. Tim Hand requested consideration of a 30 km/h speed limit on Darling Street, including the possibility of trialling reduced speed limits on sections of the corridor. He also noted community interest in cycling improvements and suggested that a lower-speed environment may reduce the need for dedicated cycling infrastructure in some locations. Council officers advised that Darling Street is a regional road and any speed limit changes would require consultation and approval from Transport for NSW. Tim Hand further commented that the existing priority bicycle network map was outdated and requested that community cycling organisations be given an opportunity to participate in any future review of the network. The Chairperson accepted a more detailed written submission for inclusion in the consultation process. Public Speaker Tim Hand left the meeting at approximately 11:16am. The Forum then considered the final draft LATM study and the matters raised by community representatives. Members generally supported the direction of the study, including the proposed traffic calming measures, pedestrian crossings, shared zones and speed reduction initiatives. The Representative for Kobi Shetty MP , Member for Balmain expressed support for the proposed shared zones and raised concerns regarding pedestrian safety around the Balmain East Ferry Wharf area. She noted the potential for vehicle and pedestrian conflicts at locations with high pedestrian activity and suggested further investigation of treatments that would improve safety where shared-zones may not be feasible. The Representative also raised accessibility concerns at Thames Street, noting that vehicles regularly obstruct kerb ramps, making access difficult for people using wheelchairs or prams. The possibility of physical treatments to prevent parking adjacent to kerb ramps was discussed. Additional bicycle parking facilities were also requested at ferry wharves, particularly near Balmain East Wharf, including consideration of shared-bike parking facilities. Council officers advised that accessibility requirements, including kerb ramps and safe access points, would be considered during the detailed design stage. Residents would also have opportunities to raise accessibility concerns through the consultation process and detailed design review. Forum members discussed the proposed indented parking bays at Mansfield Street, Wallace Street and Queens Place. Concerns were raised regarding the allocation of additional space to vehicle parking. Council officers explained that these locations had been identified because vehicles were already parking on footpaths and that shared-zone treatments were not considered appropriate under existing design requirements. The proposed upgrade at Loyalty Square was supported. Forum members identified a potential conflict between proposed landscape islands and future bicycle parking opportunities. Council officers advised that these matters could be addressed during detailed design and that investigations were already underway into converting suitable kerbside spaces into bicycle parking. The Representative for Member for Balmain also raised concerns regarding access around Gallimore Avenue, including pedestrian access from a staircase connection and parking impacts affecting nearby driveways. Council officers advised that these matters could be reviewed during detailed design and, where appropriate, investigated separately from the broader LATM process. The Representative f or IWBC requested that the bicycle network be reviewed alongside the LATM implementation process to ensure cycling routes remain appropriate following traffic changes. He also sought consideration of additional contraflow bicycle access in selected one-way streets. Council officers advised that any proposed bicycle access arrangements would require individual assessment due to width constraints, blind corners and safety considerations. Forum members suggested that the assessment of bicycle-permitted one-way streets should occur as part of the LATM implementation process rather than being deferred to a later stage. Council officers agreed that relevant streets could be reviewed as part of the next phase of the project. The Forum supported the recommendations and endorsed the Final Draft Birchgrove–Balmain East Local Area Traffic Management (LATM) Study for public exhibition. The Forum requested that matters relating to speed management, bicycle parking, cycling network review, accessibility improvements, shared-zone design, ferry wharf access, Gallimore Avenue access issues and bicycle access in one-way streets be considered during detailed design, community consultation and subsequent project review processes. RECOMMENDATION 1. That the Final Draft Birchgrove-Balmain East Local Area Traffic Management (LATM) Study be endorsed for community consultation. 2. That the report be placed on Public Exhibition, providing a minimum 28 days for community feedback and the results be reported back to the Local Transport Forum. LTF0926(1) Item 3 Darling Street, Balmain - Multi-Event Global Traffic Management Plan - (Baludarri-Balmain Ward/ Balmain Electorate/ Leichhardt PAC) SUMMARY On 16 June 2025 the Local Traffic Committee approved in-principle a multi-event global Traffic Management Plan (TMP) for the closure of Darling Street between Montague Street and Booth Street, Balmain. The TMP was approved for a period of five (5) years until 2029, with the inaugural event ‘Festival of Balmain’ successfully held on 30 November 2025. The purpose of the program is to help secure a brighter future for our communities by unlocking more walkable, safer, and activated neighbourhoods. Preparation is underway for a multi-event on Darling Street between Eaton Street and Montague Street, Balmain. The global TMP will be used for future events at this location, with the first inaugural event held on 30 November 2025, and the next to be held on Sunday 29 November 2026. The event components may include a variety of activities, such as market stalls, themed displays, food trucks, tables and chairs and entertainment. Local commercial cafes and restaurants may have the opportunity to expand outdoor seating numbers to increase trading and enhance the specific event. The event will impact surrounding streets within the Balmain area. The TMP was prepared to outline the effects on the road network, parking, pedestrian and bicycle routes, emergency routes and access to local properties and businesses. The inaugural event was successfully held on 30 November 2025, which was positively received by the community. This report contains amendments to the TMP as a number of recommendations were adopted into the report from the 2025 event. OFFICERS RECOMMENDATION That the amendments to the multi-event global Traffic Management Plan (TMP) for Darling Street between Montague Street and Eaton Street, Balmain, be approved for 29 November 2026, subject to the following conditions: 1. The event organisers notify the community including residents and businesses of the proposed event, changes to traffic and parking in the area; 2. All barricades and necessary signposting shall be provided by the event organisers and maintained during the period of the event by TfNSW-accredited marshals, or Police engaged by the applicant; 3. All traffic control facilities are to be installed in accordance with Australian Standard 1742.3; 4. The event organiser shall indemnify Inner West Council against all claims for damage or injury that may result from the activity or occupation of part of the public way during the activity. The event organiser must provide documentary evidence of public risk insurance cover of at least $20,000,000 indemnifying Council; 5. The event organiser shall be responsible for the reimbursement for the cost of repair of any damage caused to the public way, or as a result of the activities; 6. The applicant notify Transit Systems of the proposed event, including changes to impacted public bus services; and 7. The applicant apply and obtain a Road Occupation Licence from Transport for NSW for the proposed event. LTF0926(1) Item 5 Moore Street, Leichhardt - Proposed Short Term Parking (Gulgadya-Leichhardt/Balmain Electorate/Leichhardt PAC) SUMMARY Council is proposing a 11m length ‘1/2P parking 8am-6pm Mon-Fri, 8:30am-12:30pm Sat’ zone on the northern side of Moore Street adjacent to Nos. 87-89 and 99 Moore Street, Leichhardt, to improve short-term parking opportunities for visitors. The proposal is in response to concerns regarding high rates of long-term parking in this area, resulting in limited parking turnover. Community consultation on this proposal was undertaken with letters sent to 162 properties near this location. There were 16 submissions received, with feedback ranging from resident parking impacts to suggestions of a resident parking scheme. As the proposal impacts approximately two parking spaces, its impact to the surround area is considered minimal while maintaining existing parking conditions for the surrounding community. OFFICERS RECOMMENDATION That the proposed 11m length ‘1/2P 8am-6pm Mon-Fri, 8:30am-12:30pm Sat’ on the northern side of Moore Street, Leichhardt at the common boundary alignment of No. 87-89 and No.99 Moore Street be approved. LTF ADVICE Public speaker Anne McLellan entered the meeting at 11:16am Ms Anne McLellan advised that the proposed parking changes would not adequately address the underlying parking pressures and believed the proposal could potentially worsen parking availability for nearby residents. She stated that long-term parking by employees was the primary cause of parking congestion, resulting in difficulties for residents, visitors and customers seeking parking. Ms Anne McLellan referred to the broader resident parking scheme consultation undertaken in 2025 and expressed concern that the outcome may not have accurately reflected the views of residents living closest to Moore Street. She supported reconsideration of a broader resident parking scheme incorporating 1P or 2P restrictions and noted that such an approach would provide greater parking turnover and better address the parking issues experienced in the precinct. She also highlighted issue of parking by boats, caravans and commercial vehicles as contributing factors. Public speaker Anne McLellan left the meeting at 11:22am Council officers advised that resident parking schemes are subject to a formal consultation process and that responses are assessed from eligible properties. Forum members acknowledged the broader parking concerns raised by Anne McLellan including the level of commercial activity in the area and the need to improve parking turnover. The Forum also noted that the current proposal impacts two parking spaces and is intended to provide short-term visitor parking opportunities. RECOMMENDATION That the proposed 11m length ‘1/2P 8am-6pm Mon-Fri, 8:30am-12:30pm Sat’ on the northern side of Moore Street, Leichhardt at the common boundary alignment of No. 87-89 and No.99 Moore Street be approved. LTF0926(1) Item 8 Victoria Road, Marrickville – Pedestrian Crossing Investigation (Midjuburi-Marrickville Ward / Summer Hill Electorate / Inner West PAC) SUMMARY Council at its meeting held on 19 May 2026 raised a Notice of Motion requesting an investigation into providing a pedestrian crossing facility on Victoria Road, between Sydenham Road and Chalder Street, Marrickville. This report provides the outcome of this investigation. Pedestrian and vehicle volume data was collected and assessed against relevant Council and TfNSW guidelines and policies. The pedestrian and vehicle volumes assessed did not meet the volume warrants of either TfNSW or the Inner West Council’s Pedestrian Crossing Warrant Policy and therefore with exception of monitoring this section of Victoria Road, no further action should be undertaken at present. OFFICE RECOMMENDATION 1. That the report below be received and noted. 2. That a proposed pedestrian crossing facility on Victoria Road, Marrickville between Sydenham Road and Chalder Street, Marrickville not be supported at present. 3. That a review of traffic data and possible treatments be undertaken and a report including identifying any potential developer contributions be prepared towards the end of 2027. LTF ADVIDE The Chairperson raised concerns about pedestrian safety and the timing of investigation works in the context of the Timber Yard redevelopment and the existing/complementary development activity on Victoria Road. The Forum discussed the expected increase in pedestrian activity associated with the Timber Yard development and nearby commercial frontage. The existing speed environment on Victoria Road was discussed, including whether a lower speed limit should be considered for the relevant commercial/shopping-strip environment. It was noted that this would require Transport for NSW involvement. Concern was expressed that pedestrian infrastructure should not simply be deferred until development is fully completed. The Chairperson proposed that alternative pedestrian safety treatments and technically feasible crossing locations be investigated along Victoria Road between Sydney Road and Chapel Street, including interim measures. The proposal included updated pedestrian counts and accessibility assessment before substantial occupation of the Timber Yard development and again following occupation. The Forum also sought identification of developer obligations and available developer contributions for pedestrian safety works. The Forum discussed a report timeframe and the chairperson advised that the development is expected to be completed around 2028, with staged occupation. Therefore, it was agreed that a review of traffic data and possible treatments be undertaken and a report including identifying any potential developer contributions being prepared towards the end of 2027 was considered reasonable to obtain meaningful pedestrian data while avoiding waiting until full completion. The Forum agreed that the currently assessed crossing options were not supported at this stage. RECOMMENDATION 1. That the report below be received and noted. 2. That a proposed pedestrian crossing facility on Victoria Road, Marrickville between Sydenham Road and Chalder Street, Marrickville not be supported at present. 3. That a review of traffic data and possible treatments be undertaken and a report including identifying any potential developer contributions be prepared towards the end of 2027. LTF0926(1) Item 9 On Street Bike Parking - LGA Wide September 2026 SUMMARY Share bike and food delivery use has grown rapidly across the Inner West LGA, leading to increased footpath clutter and pedestrian amenity impacts. It is recommended that Council install "Bicycle Parking Only" signage at the identified sites across the LGA. This proposal aims to convert existing kerbside restrictions into designated on-street bike parking and will improve footpath accessibility for pedestrians whilst formalising share bike operator responsibilities for compliance and maintenance. OFFICE RECOMMENDATION 1. That the installation of “Bicycle Parking Only’ signs and line marking be approved at the following locations: a) Western side of Norton Street, opposite Norton Street Plaza, Leichhardt b) Northern side of Darling Street at Loyalty Square, Balmain c) Northern side of Hastings Street next to Livingstone Road, Marrickville d) Northern side of Enfield Street next to Livingstone Road, Marrickville e) Western side of Regent Street next to Trafalgar Street, Petersham 2. That the following “Bicycle Parking Only” locations be noted as part of the 17 th August 2026 Local Transport Forum Delegation a) Southern side of Warburton Street, from 6m west of Illawarra Road to 12m west of Illawarra Road b) Northern side of Arthur Street, from 10m west of Illawarra Road to 16m west of Illawarra Road. LTF ADVICE The representative for IWBC welcomed the proposal but raised concerns that shared bicycles were occupying existing commuter bicycle parking facilities and suggested greater management of high-demand locations. Council officers advised that the proposed facilities were primarily intended to support shared bike parking, although they did not prevent use by private bicycles and that the proposal represents an initial rollout of shared bicycle parking facilities and that additional locations will be introduced in stages, including sites near public transport interchanges and railway stations. The proposed facilities are intended to reduce pressure on existing bicycle racks and improve pedestrian accessibility by relocating bicycles from footpaths to designated on-street spaces. Councilor Atkins raised concerns regarding shared bicycles around popular destinations, including local cafés, and suggested that operators should be using location data to identify areas where dedicated bicycle parking may be required. She also highlighted the importance of rider education, particularly where bicycles are left obstructing kerb ramps, pedestrian crossings and accessible paths of travel. The Forum members noted that designated parking and geo-fenced shared-bike parking areas operating in parts of Balmain appeared to reduce inappropriate bicycle parking and improve compliance and suggested U-rail at the proposed bicycle parking locations on Norton Street and at Loyalty Square to provide a visual parking cue and protect parked bicycles from vehicle maneuvers.
